senses.gloss:
--seven in number, one above the other like several umbrellas spread over. To the usual seven are added वैकुण्ठ and Golokam;
1: Br. II. १९. १५५-6; २१. १९. २१; III. ४१. ५४-5.
the fourteen sthalas or places of which seven are कृत and seven are अकृत; भूः and other six are कृतस्; the अकृतस् are प्राकृतस्; पृथ्वी, अन्तरिक्ष, दिव्य and महर्लोकस् are known as अर्णवकस् or which stand until आभूतसम्प्लव; जन, तप and सब्य are ज्ञानलोकस्; व्यक्तलोकस् are भूः, भुवः, स्वः, मह, जन, तप and सत्य (Brahma); their residents are given, those attaining Brahmaloka (सत्य) do not have rebirth.
2: वा. १०१. १०-39; Vi. I. २२. ८०; V. 2. १६.

--the world of सान्तानिकस् and आदिदेवस् of seven गुणस्; above and below them are another seven गुणस्; after which come the devas and earth; from them are rains which invigorate the world. वा. ७१. ५७. [page३-125+ ३७]
--the lordship of a quarter of the world; Yama became a लोकपाल by pleasing शिव. M. ११. २०.
--the mother goddesses being the १४ daughters of दक्ष, married to कश्यप. Br. III. 3. ५५-6; 7. ४६९. [page३-126+ २८]
--south of नागवीथि and north of लोका- loka. Br. II. २१. १०३.
(I)--the अवतार् of the Lord in the sixth द्वा- para with four learned disciples, all yogins. वा. २३. १३३.
(II)--one of the four disciples of पौष्यञ्जि Va1. ६१. ३६-7; Vi. III. 6. 6.

--Soma takes away the water drunk by the sun through नाडिस् and thus sets in motion the ज्योतिष cakram. The clouds drink from Soma and pour in as rain for six months by the heaviness of the wind; thus the waters are not wasted; once taken they are returned; from the sun comes heat, and from the moon शीतलम्। वा. ५१. १४-16.

--ईश्वर, the bridge among bridges, the holy among the holies, the Vedya among the Vedic scholars, the Prabhu among Lords, सोमभूत for beings, अग्निभूत for promoting the effulgence of Agni, मनोभूते for men, तपोभूत for tapasvins, vinaya for police men, tejas among tejasvins, vigraha among idols, and the place for journey men. Va. ९७. ४०-43.
(I)--the Mt. forming the boundary of the earth. Br. I. 1. ७८; 3. ३१; वा. ४९. १४४; ५०. १५५, १६०, २०५; १०१. १९१-2. [page३-127+ २९]

(II)--(Mt.) a chain of hills beyond the स्वा- दूदक, between the Loka where the sun shines and Aloka where he does not. The regions lighted by the sun are said to cover ५० crores of yojanas. The chain of the लोका- loka is said to occupy a fourth of the area of the globe. In the Aloka योगेश्वर-Kr2s2n2a travels.
1: भा. V. २०. ३४-42; M. १२३. ४७; १२४. ३८, ८१.
Crossed by Arjuna and कृष्ण on their way to वैकुण्ठ in search of the dead child of the ब्राह्मण of द्वारका. A. mythical mountainous belt in the south separating the visible world from the world of darkness.
3: Br. II. १५. 3; १९. १५०; २१. ५१, १०१ and १०६, १५५; III. 7. २९४; IV. 2. १९४.
१०,000 yoja- nas in height and breadth; protected by four guardians, सुधामन् and others on the four directions.
4: Vi. II. 4. ९४; 8. ८२-3.
